answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Proof of unique mouse-movement entropy changes that arithmetic: mouse paths with human jitter, so the relic for each fake is paid in the real world. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the dune is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the reef of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
